samples.why_account: The annual report names faster application retirement and cloud migration among 2026 priorities.
samples.why_offer: Redesign an end-to-end business service and its operating model so an accountable enterprise sponsor can realise and sustain measurable customer and operational value.
samples.why_now: Explore timing with the owner; no urgency inferred.
samples.entry_play: Start from a customer outcome, not the next technology platform. Which end-to-end service outcome is materially constrained, and who owns the benefits after launch?
samples.next_test: Would process simplification and clearer ownership achieve the outcome without an enterprise technology programme?

value_case.disconfirmation: No material service gap, no accountable benefit owner, or a simpler process-only change has a better evidenced value case
measures: End-to-end service completion and time-to-serve
Repeat contacts and avoidable rework
Sustained adoption and benefits-owner acceptance
mechanisms: Less avoidable journey rework and failure demand
Improved service completion and customer experience
More effective allocation of change investment
value_case.method: Compare customer-approved baseline and future-state service outcomes; monetise only evidenced volume × attributable unit-cost change, less implementation, transition and recurring operating costs. Avoid double counting with other programmes.
value_case.status: Unvalued until customer baseline, attribution, costs and approval are established

samples.why_account: The strategy makes enterprise data enablement a stated AI priority.

samples.why_now: Explore timing with the owner; no urgency inferred.
samples.entry_play: The opportunity is a better business process, not more AI usage. Which process outcome warrants changing work allocation, controls and accountability?
samples.next_test: Would a rules-based or process-only alternative achieve the same outcome with lower total risk and cost?

costs: Runtime, evaluation, human review and control operations
value_case.disconfirmation: AI does not beat the simpler baseline, review effort offsets gains, or an acceptable accountable operating model cannot be established
measures: Task quality and exception/rework rates
Human review effort and service completion

Less avoidable handling and rework where demonstrated

samples.why_account: Lloyds describes built-in Envoy controls and monitoring. A missing-control or greenfield-platform pitch is weakened; effectiveness needs customer validation.
samples.why_offer: Improve an enterprise’s ability to protect and recover a critical business service through a prioritised, evidenced cyber control, resilience and assurance programme.

samples.entry_play: Protect the service outcome; do not start by assuming another security tool is needed. Which authorised scenario could impair this service despite the controls already in place?

value_case.disconfirmation: Current controls demonstrably meet risk and recovery objectives, or proposed changes do not improve the customer-approved scenario
measures: Tested recovery and escalation completion
Critical dependency/control ownership coverage
Evidence-backed remediation closure and assurance rework

Less duplicated assurance and remediation effort
More defensible risk prioritisation and recovery decisions
value_case.method: Use owner-approved risk and service-impact scenarios; quantify only supported exposure and control costs, with assumptions and ranges if later evidenced. Do not turn an unobserved breach probability or avoided fine into a promised saving.
value_case.status: Unvalued until customer baseline, attribution, costs and approval are established

samples.why_account: The annual report names faster application retirement and cloud migration among 2026 priorities.
samples.why_offer: Modernise a complex application estate through a defensible retain, retire, rehost, replatform, refactor or replace strategy while preserving critical-service continuity and accountable value.
samples.why_now: Explore timing with the owner; no urgency inferred.
samples.entry_play: The valuable decision is where to retain, retire or change the estate safely, not a blanket rewrite. Which business services and supplier dependencies constrain the programme, and what evidence would justify each treatment option?
samples.next_test: Can a supported upgrade, retention or retirement remove the constraint with less transition risk?

costs: Dual run, support extensions and contractual exit
Operational readiness, rollback and long-term maintenance
value_case.disconfirmation: Retention or a smaller upgrade has better evidenced whole-life value, or continuity and rights cannot be established
measures: Verified retired run/support costs and contract obligations
Service parity, reconciliation and recovery observations
Lead time and dependency/ownership closure
mechanisms: Retire demonstrably unnecessary run and support cost
Improve change capacity and remove measured dependency friction
Reduce supported obsolescence and transition exposure
value_case.method: Compare whole-life retain and change options including support extensions, licences, vendor/IP rights, dual run, migration, reconciliation, exit and support. Count retired cost only when obligations actually end; avoid blanket cloud or rewrite savings.
value_case.status: Unvalued until customer baseline, attribution, costs and approval are established

measures: Verified additional social outcomes within a stated contract/boundary

Do not infer contract wins, automatic carbon savings or regulatory acceptance.
value_case.status: Unvalued until customer baseline, attribution, costs and approval are established
